extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, PTAB stakeholders, petitioners and patent owners, patent attorneys, and participants in USPTO rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Notice withdrawing a proposed rule that would have revised PTAB rules of practice governing the Director's and PTAB's discretion to institute inter partes and post-grant reviews, including briefing of discretionary denial issues, 35 U.S.C. 325(d) considerations, handling parallel/serial petitions, and termination following settlement. The page summarizes what the proposed rule would have changed and states the withdrawal and its rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of practice for IPR and PGR proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the rules of practice for inter partes review (IPR) and post-grant review (PGR) proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) that the Director and, by delegation, the PTAB use in exercising discretion to institute IPRs and PGRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule would have modified and built on existing PTAB precedent and guidance concerning institution discretion. (The proposal that would have implemented these revisions is withdrawn as of October 17, 2025.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing of discretionary denial issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a separate briefing process for discretionary institution arguments and for briefing discretionary denial issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule 'provided a separate briefing process for discretionary institution arguments' to address discretionary denial issues; the document notes this as one of the procedural changes the NPRM would have implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: 325(d) considerations (same or substantially the same art/arguments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish rules for 35 U.S.C. 325(d) considerations regarding petitions that implicate the same or substantially the same art or arguments previously presented to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule would have modified PTAB precedent and guidance concerning petitions 'implicating the same or substantially the same art or arguments previously presented to the Office,' i.e., 325(d)-type considerations for declining institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instituting parallel and serial petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Set rules of practice for instituting proceedings when petitions are parallel or serial and address how serial and parallel petitions should be treated in institution decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule 'modified and built on existing PTAB precedent and guidance concerning serial petitions, parallel petitions, and petitions implicating the same or substantially the same art or arguments previously presented to the Office.' Specific procedures were described in the NPRM (now withdrawn).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination due to settlement agreement; alignment of procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Align procedures before and after institution regarding settlement agreements and termination of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule 'aligned the procedures before and after institution regarding settlement agreements and termination.' The notice explains this alignment as part of the procedural changes the NPRM would have implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking procedural elements and stakeholder comment process
rubrics_metrics.description: 60-day public comment period and public availability of comments on regulations.gov; USPTO received extensive stakeholder submissions which inform rulemaking decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule's comment period ran from April 19, 2024 to June 18, 2024. The USPTO received more than 3,900 submissions (110 unique comments). Comments are publicly available at www.regulations.gov/docket/PTO-P-2023-0048. The notice states the rule is withdrawn to evaluate future actions in light of administration priorities and welcomes continued stakeholder feedback.
